rule: section 2.8 (forum and dispute-forum allocations owe no counterparty performance -- v0.68, REVIEWER-RULED, this segment is the motivating case); with sections 3.2.1 and 8.8/3.5 disposing of the other three sentences, leaving ZERO obligation-bearing clauses and so failing section 2's 1-3 band as well
reason:
Submission-to-jurisdiction / waiver-of-venue boilerplate. FOUR sentences, offsets verified by execution via corpus.split_sentences(), and NOT ONE is obligation-bearing.

S1 [0:48] '(a) Submission to Jurisdiction; Waiver of Venue.' -- a heading, no modal, no clause.

S2 [49:510] THE ONLY LIVE CANDIDATE, and the segment's reason for existing in the record: 'Each Party hereto agrees that any action, proceeding or claim it commences against the other Party pursuant to this Agreement shall be brought [page artifact] in the courts of the United States for the Southern District of New York...'. EXCLUDED under section 2.8 on the ground that a forum allocation OWES NO COUNTERPARTY PERFORMANCE -- it fixes the legal position of a dispute that may never arise rather than requiring either party to render anything to the other in the course of performing the agreement. No deliverable, no deadline, no correlative party owed a performance; a party that never commences an action can never fail to comply.

TWO NEARER-LOOKING GROUNDS WERE CONSIDERED AND BOTH SET ASIDE AS NON-DECIDING, recorded here so a future reader does not reconstruct the ruling from the wrong one.
(a) NOT the thing-subject ground. S2's operative subject is 'any action, proceeding or claim', a non-party, which is what C10-029 and C04-163 were excluded on -- but that ground is UNAVAILABLE here: C04-03 and C14-05 are LOCKED ITEMS whose spans are thing-subject agentless passives, so a non-party grammatical subject has never been sufficient to exclude.
(b) NOT the taxonomy gap. Under the competing reading the performance is 'bringing an action in a named court' and NO member of ACTIONS denotes it (COMPLY, read that way, would swallow any duty whatever and collapse the taxonomy). That observation is REAL and DOES NOT DECIDE: section 8.8 exists so a genuine taxonomy gap is annotated with the nearest verb and TAGGED rather than excluded, and section 3.7 requires known-gap forms to be annotated normally rather than avoided. Had this clause owed a counterparty performance the absent verb would have made it an action_not_in_taxonomy ITEM, not an exclusion.
(c) NOT section 2.5 either, which is the trap this ruling is written to avoid. Section 2.5's PRINCIPLE ('a future state worth monitoring') fits comfortably, but its OPERATIVE TRIGGER is unreviewable discretion (section 2.5.1's 'in its sole business judgment'), which a forum clause has none of -- and section 8.8.4 already corrected a disposition that stretched section 2.5 across exactly this distance. Hence a new section rather than a citation.

THE COUNTER-READING, recorded rather than defeated. S2 carries 'shall', its operative verb 'be brought' is a performance rather than a copula, and a filing in the wrong court is observable -- so it can fairly be read as a conditional duty (if you sue, sue here) whose breach a court itself remedies by dismissal or transfer. On that reading the item would carry obligor: ABSENT and obligee: ABSENT under section 3.5.3 ('Each Party' is the subject of 'agrees', 'it' the agent of 'commences'; neither occupies a core argument slot of 'shall be brought'), making it the SECOND both-ABSENT item after C14-06. What decides against it is that the constraint runs to the FORUM rather than to the counterparty.

S3 [511:1127] 'Each Party HEREBY irrevocably and unconditionally submits to the jurisdiction ... and irrevocably and unconditionally WAIVES ...' -- section 3.2.1's present-tense self-executing performative class, whose own rule text names 'hereby waives' in terms. Takes full effect at execution, so no future state remains to monitor.

S4 [1128:1387] 'Each Party agrees that a final non-appealable judgment ... shall be conclusive and binding and may be enforced in other jurisdictions ...' -- subject is 'a final non-appealable judgment', a thing; 'shall be conclusive and binding' is COPULAR STATUS (section 8.8) and 'may be enforced' a right on that same non-party subject. Same class as C10-029 (severability, no party subject anywhere) and C04-163.

COST, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED, and it is why this ruling is about the record and not about a number: FIGURE-NEUTRAL on every published figure -- in-force criterion 2 5/10 = 50.0%, all-items 7/15 = 46.7%, K 14/32, A 7/27, 60 items over 35 segments, all unchanged and confirmed by a real run_scoring.run() AFTER the ruling (15 items scored, 45 cassette-unscoreable, teardown clean) rather than hand-computed. STATED PRECISELY: the run was made ONCE, after. The pre-ruling figures are the published ones the committed suite already reproduces, and an exclusion adds no item, so there is no mechanism by which this change could move them -- but that is an argument, not a second run. THAT IS TRUE OF THE COMPETING READING TOO, which is the honest half: an annotated item would have carried action_not_in_taxonomy AND corpus_artifact_in_span (the page header sits at [192:270], wedged between 'shall be brought' ending 191 and 'in the courts of' starting 270, so no span stating the complete obligation can avoid it), both REPRESENTATIONAL, so section 9.1 excludes the item from the in-force denominator on either tag alone. NEITHER DISPOSITION COULD HAVE MOVED THE HEADLINE FIGURE, so the ruling could not have been reached for to protect one.
observations: FORWARD GUIDANCE, so the next instance is decided by citation rather than re-litigated: the class is 9 instances across 9 documents -- C02-084, C03-161, C04-172, C12-016, C13-047, C15-058, C22-043, E05-026, E08-041 -- essentially one per document, forum clauses being universal commercial boilerplate. That is the section 14.4 'repeated uncertainty is a missing rule' shape rather than a per-item call, and it is why this became an amendment. Measured over the rebuilt 1,547-segment pool by a screen GATED on C04-172 being flagged before any count was read off it; preserved at evals/goldens/holdout/forum_allocation/screen.py.

THE SCREEN'S OWN ERROR RATE IS PUBLISHED RATHER THAN PATCHED AWAY: 25 raw flags, 16 hand-rejected, a 64% override rate. The screen is LOOSE and the hand pass is LOAD-BEARING; the raw 25 must never be quoted as the class size. Rejections include severability clauses (C05-076, E03-059), a definition (C04-007), a notice ADDRESS block with a docket stamp (C06-100) and eight bankruptcy-sale provisions, each with its reason recorded in the script.

A NEIGHBOURING SHAPE DELIBERATELY LEFT UNRULED, named so it is not swept in by analogy: three further flags -- C04-171, C13-046, C14-148 -- are PARTY-SUBJECT MAY rights to refer a dispute ('either Party may submit such Dispute to a court of competent jurisdiction'). A named party in the subject slot exercising a right is not a thing-subject allocation of where a dispute lies, and whether such a right is annotable is a different question. Section 2.8 decides only the latter. C14-148 is already measured under section 3.5.2 for an unrelated reason.

QUEUE ROW OPENED: section 10.1 F35, OPENED 2026-10-06 BY C04-172 -- does section 2.8's exclusion reach an arbitration SEAT that carries an ancillary performance? C04-172 is a PURE allocation (it names a court and nothing else), but C03-161, C12-016, C13-047 and E08-041 adopt a named institution's rules or fix an arbitrator count, and whether adopting a procedural regime is a counterparty performance is open. NOT a challenge to section 2.8, whose ruling stands on this segment's own facts; what is open is the REACH of the ground, not its correctness.

segment_text: (a) Submission to Jurisdiction; Waiver of Venue. Each Party hereto agrees that any action, proceeding or claim it commences against the other Party pursuant to this Agreement shall be brought 41 Miltenyi Biotec-Bellicum Supply Agreement (Execution Copy, March 27, 2019) in the courts of the United States for the Southern District of New York, and any appellate court from any thereof, in any action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or for recognition or enforcement of any judgment. Each Party hereby irrevocably and unconditionally submits to the jurisdiction of the State of New York Courts and irrevocably and unconditionally waives, to the fullest extent permitted by law, any objection which it may now or hereafter have to the laying of the venue of any such suit, action or proceeding brought in any such court, any claim that any such suit, action or proceeding brought in such a court has been brought in an inconvenient forum and the right to object, with respect to any such suit, action or proceeding brought in any such court, that such court does not have jurisdiction over such Party. Each Party agrees that a final non-appealable judgment in any such suit, action or proceeding in such a court shall be conclusive and binding and may be enforced in other jurisdictions by suit on the judgment or in any other manner provided by Applicable Law.
